items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The biography in The New Grove Dictionary of Jazz lists that you learned tap- dancing, or were a tap-dancer with a barrelhouse pianist, Speckled Red. You said that you played with him.

ctx.x: With Roy Knapp? I studied with him for about three years. I gained a lot of knowledge, and it gave me a chance to go to Chicago, take my lesson from him, then stay over a day or two, and like I said before, go to catch Cab Calloway, Gene Krupa, Tommy Dorsey, Duke, Basie. I caught all of them.

The biography in The New Grove Dictionary of Jazz lists that you learned tap- dancing, or were a tap-dancer with a barrelhouse pianist, Speckled Red. You said that you played with him. Did you also – is that an accurate account? Were you also a tap dancer?

All the drummers during that era – Jo Jones, for example, Buddy Rich – Steve Gadd was a Mouseketeer. They all tap-danced. They told jokes. Because when you played the theaters, you did everything. You were m.c. You had a dance routine. You had a dance routine called a b.s. chorus. It was nothing but a series of taps. That’s how Baby Lawrence, Teddy Hale, Bunny Briggs – that’s where all those guys came up, from the tap-dance era. My sister Mary – full sister – taught me how to tap-dance. She taught me the…
